---
title: Archetypes and controls
guide-section: "Generating studies"
---

An *archetype* is a study type: a design (arms, visits, periods or cohorts), a model of how
subjects' courses unfold, and the SDTM and ADaM datasets a study of that type would have. Its
*controls* are the settings you can change, each with a default, so `tf.study("vaccine")` alone
gives a complete, plausible study.

The split between the two is deliberate. The archetype fixes what makes a study of its kind
correct: which domains it has, how its visits are planned, how responses are assessed and how the
analysis datasets are derived. The controls expose what varies from one study of that kind to the
next, stated in the terms a protocol or a statistical analysis plan would use: the treatment
duration, the expected effect, the dropout rate, the allocation ratio.

## The archetypes

`tf.archetypes()` lists them with one-line descriptions:

```{python}
import trialforge as tf

tf.archetypes()
```

| Archetype | What it simulates |
|---|---|
| `parallel_continuous` | Randomized, double-blind study with a continuous endpoint: `type_2_diabetes` (HbA1c), `hypertension` (SBP) or `obesity` (weight); placebo-controlled, or active-controlled with a non-inferiority margin |
| `dose_ranging_ph2` | Phase 2 dose-ranging study (placebo and several doses) with a sigmoid Emax dose-response; the truth manifest refits the Emax model |
| `cv_outcomes` | Event-driven cardiovascular outcomes trial: recurrent MI and stroke, CV death and competing non-CV death in CE; time to first MACE and its components in ADTTE; the study ends at a target number of events |
| `cns_alzheimers` | Placebo-controlled study in mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease: ADAS-Cog (11) items (FT) from an IRT model of cognitive decline, prorated totals and LOCF analysis |
| `oncology_solid_tumor` | Randomized solid-tumor study: RECIST 1.1 tumor assessments, confirmed response, progression and death, calibrated to target medians, hazard ratios and response rates |
| `heme_lymphoma` | Randomized study in relapsed or refractory DLBCL: Lugano 2014 lesions, CT- and PET-CT-based responses, ADRS, PFS and OS calibrated to targets |
| `phase1_sad_mad` | First-in-human single or multiple ascending dose study in healthy volunteers: dose cohorts with placebo, intensive PK (1- or 2-compartment population model), NCA, dose proportionality |
| `crossover_be` | Crossover bioequivalence (2x2 or 2x2x4 replicate) or food-effect study: periods and washouts, per-period PK and NCA, the BE analysis of AUC and Cmax |
| `dose_escalation` | Phase 1 dose escalation in advanced solid tumors with a 3+3, BOIN or mTPI-2 design: cohorts chosen from DLTs, the DLT-evaluable population and the selected MTD |
| `pediatric_growth` | Once-weekly vs. daily growth hormone in children: height, weight and BMI on the CDC 2000 charts, growth z-scores and percentiles, annualized height velocity |
| `respiratory_exacerbation` | Placebo-controlled COPD study: moderate and severe exacerbations in CE (negative binomial counts), FEV1 in RE |
| `vaccine` | Placebo-controlled one- or two-dose vaccine study: neutralizing antibody titers (IS), 7-day reactogenicity diaries (FACE, CE, VS) |
| `ophthalmology` | Active-controlled non-inferiority study of intravitreal Drug A in neovascular AMD: study and fellow eye visual acuity and retinal thickness |

Every archetype has the trial design datasets and the domains any study has: demographics (DM),
subject elements and visits (SE, SV), exposure (EX) and disposition (DS), with ADSL. All but three
also have the safety domains, adverse events (AE, with SUPPAE), concomitant medications (CM),
medical history (MH), labs (LB) and vital signs (VS), with ADAE, ADLB and ADVS, and add their own
domains to them. The oncology archetypes and `cv_outcomes` focus on efficacy: tumor data (TU, TR,
RS) with ADRS and ADTTE, or clinical events (CE) with ADTTE.

## Controls

`tf.controls()` lists an archetype's controls, each with a description and its default:

```{python}
tf.controls("parallel_continuous")
```

Pass controls to `tf.study()` as keyword arguments. Anything you leave out keeps its default:

```{python}
trial = tf.study("parallel_continuous", n=200, seed=1, indication="obesity", weeks=52)
trial.controls
```

`Study.controls` is the full set the study used, defaults included, so it records the whole request.

Controls are checked before anything is generated. A misspelled name is an error that lists the
valid ones, and so is a value of the wrong type or out of range:

```{python}
try:
    tf.study("parallel_continuous", n=200, seed=1, wekks=52)
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
```

Values are checked against each other too, where they interact: an oncology study's progression
median must be shorter than its survival median, and its data cutoff later than the end of
enrollment.

```{python}
try:
    tf.study("oncology_solid_tumor", n=200, seed=1, pfs_median_months=20, os_median_months=15)
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
```

## Indication presets

`parallel_continuous` (and `dose_ranging_ph2`, which shares its design) takes an `indication` that
chooses a preset. A preset is more than an endpoint: it sets the population and the study around
it, so that a type 2 diabetes study looks like one and an obesity study like another.

| Preset | Endpoint | Change at end of treatment (placebo, active) | Population |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type_2_diabetes` | HbA1c (LB, `HBA1C`) | -0.2, -1.0 % | Adults with HbA1c 7.0–10.5% at screening, most on background metformin |
| `hypertension` | Systolic blood pressure (VS, `SYSBP`) | -4, -12 mmHg | Adults with sitting SBP 140–180 mmHg at screening |
| `obesity` | Body weight (VS, `WEIGHT`) | -1.5, -8 kg | Adults with a BMI of at least 30 kg/m^2^ |

Beyond the endpoint, each preset sets the age and BMI distributions, the baseline means of its
analytes and the eligibility criteria in TI, the medical history every subject has and the
background medication in CM, the trial title and objective in TS, and which adverse events are more
common on the active drug (gastrointestinal events for type 2 diabetes and obesity, dizziness and
peripheral edema for hypertension). The effect develops over the first weeks of treatment, at a
pace that suits the endpoint.

Other controls refine a preset rather than replace it. `change=[-4, -11]` keeps the hypertension
study and changes only the effect; `comparator="active"` makes the control arm an active comparator
(with equal effects unless `change` says otherwise), and `ni_margin` adds a non-inferiority analysis
to the truth manifest:

```{python}
ni = tf.study(
    "parallel_continuous", n=200, seed=1, indication="hypertension", comparator="active", ni_margin=3
)
ni.truth["non_inferiority"]
```

## Controls that change the design

Some controls change a study's structure, not just its numbers:

| Archetype | Control | Choices |
|---|---|---|
| `crossover_be` | `design`{.gd-no-link} | `2x2` (TR/RT), `2x2x4` (TRTR/RTRT, replicate) or `food_effect` (fed/fasted) |
| `phase1_sad_mad` | `part` | `sad` (one dose) or `mad` (once-daily dosing for `mad_days`) |
| `phase1_sad_mad` | `compartments` | a 1- or 2-compartment PK model |
| `dose_escalation` | `method` | `3+3`, `boin` or `mtpi2` |
| `vaccine` | `doses` | a one- or two-dose primary series |
| `parallel_continuous` | `comparator` | `placebo` or `active` |
| Several archetypes | `ratio` | the allocation ratio, in arm order |
| Fixed-duration archetypes | `weeks` | the treatment duration, which sets the visit schedule |

## Controls that are clinical targets

Some controls are clinical targets rather than model parameters: a median survival, a hazard ratio
or a response rate. trialforge calibrates its latent model so that the study is expected to hit the
target, and the [truth manifest](04-truth.qmd) reports the target next to what the generated data
realized. The oncology controls are of this kind:

```{python}
[c.name for c in tf.controls("oncology_solid_tumor")]
```

The medians, hazard ratios and response rates are targets; the Weibull shapes and the correlation
between progression and death are parameters of the model that shape the curves around them.

Elsewhere, a control is the population value of what the study's analysis estimates: a mean change
from baseline, a geometric mean titer, an exacerbation rate ratio, a geometric mean ratio of AUC.
These need no calibration, and the truth manifest reports them as targets in the same way.

## Modifiers of event-driven studies

`oncology_solid_tumor` and `heme_lymphoma` take a crossover-on-progression modifier
(`crossover_prob`, `crossover_os_hr`): control subjects who progress may switch to Drug A, in a
`CONTINUATION TREATMENT` element, and their survival follows the Drug A hazard from then on.
Crossover happens after progression, so it leaves the progression-free survival calibration
unchanged but dilutes the observed overall survival difference, as it does in real studies.

Event-driven studies can also be cut early. `interim_months` on the oncology archetypes and
`interim_events` on `cv_outcomes` give an interim snapshot of the same study, with the same subjects
and courses, cut at the earlier date. Subjects randomized after the cut are absent, TS records the
interim cutoff, and `trial.truth["interim"]` reports it. Generating the final analysis and an
interim with the same seed and controls gives two cuts of one study, as a sponsor would see them.

## Other arguments

- `n`: the number of randomized subjects (300 by default). In `phase1_sad_mad` it is split evenly
across the dose cohorts. In `dose_escalation` it is the maximum sample size: a 3+3 design stops
once it has found the maximum tolerated dose, so it may treat fewer.
- `seed`{.gd-no-link}: the root seed (see [Reproducibility](09-reproducibility.qmd)).
- `studyid`{.gd-no-link}: `STUDYID`; each archetype has a default, such as `SIMPAR01`.
- `output`: the DataFrame type of `Study.sdtm` and `Study.adam`.
- `defects`{.gd-no-link}: data-quality defects to inject (see [Seeded defects](07-defects.qmd)).
